checker.desc: Enter your income and assets for a quick check of basic livelihood security eligibility
checker.noteSimple: This is a simplified check and may differ from the actual decision.

checker.emptyLine1: Enter your income and assets on the left,
checker.formula1: Recognized income = assessed income + income-converted assets
checker.formula2: Assessed income = actual income - household-specific expenses - earned income deduction (30%)
checker.formula3: Income-converted assets = (assets - basic property allowance - debt) × conversion rate
checker.rates: Conversion rates: general property 4.17%/mo, financial assets 6.26%/mo, car 100%/mo

medianIncome.source: Source: Ministry of Health and Welfare notice on standard median income and livelihood/medical benefit thresholds — No. 2025-135 for 2026, No. 2026-157 for 2027 (issued 29 Jul 2026). Each year's values apply from 1 January.
medianIncome.upcoming: The {year} standard median income applies from 1 January {year}. Applications and reviews now use the {current} values.
medianIncome.checkerYear: Assessed with the {year} standard median income (applies from 1 January each year).
checkerNotes: A home you live in and rental deposits are actually converted as residential assets (1.04% a month, within regional limits). Entering them as general assets (4.17% a month) can overstate recognized income (MOHW notice No. 2019-188).

Cars are converted at 100% a month here. Passenger cars under 2,000cc that are 10+ years old or worth under KRW 5M use the general-asset rate (4.17% a month) instead (MOHW notice No. 2025-204, Annex 2).
medianIncome.title: Median Income Reference

whatIs.title: What is Median Income?
whatIs.description: The standard median income is the midpoint of national household income announced annually by the Ministry of Health and Welfare. It serves as the qualification threshold for various government welfare programs including basic livelihood benefits and housing support.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Select the year (2023-2027). The year currently in force is selected by default.
Review median income by household size (1-6 persons).
Check amounts at various percentage thresholds (32%-300%).
See which government welfare programs each threshold qualifies for.

tips.title: Tips
items: Livelihood benefits: 32%, medical: 40%, housing: 48%, education: 50% of median income.
Median income uses pre-tax income. The 'recognized income' calculation differs from simple salary.
Median income increases yearly - check again even if you didn't qualify last year.

items.a: KRW 2,564,238 a month for 1-person households and KRW 6,494,738 for 4-person households, up 6.51% year on year for 4 persons (MOHW notice No. 2025-135).

KRW 6,929,885 for 4 persons (+6.70%) and KRW 2,736,042 for 1 person, decided by the Central Living Security Committee on 28 Jul 2026 and applied from 1 Jan 2027 (MOHW notice No. 2026-157). The livelihood benefit threshold (32%) is KRW 2,217,563 for 4 persons and KRW 875,533 for 1 person.
Recognized income = Income assessment + Asset-to-income conversion. Use the Bokjiro (bokjiro.go.kr) simulation tool for precise calculation.

items.q: What benefits are available at 100% median income?
items.a: Each program sets its own threshold. For example, the youth monthly rent support requires the parents' household income to be at or below 100% of median income. Some programs, like the child tax credit, use total household income (under KRW 70M) instead of median income, so check each program's notice.
